evidence.quote: The dataset was manually handcrafted, limiting the diversity of problem types and complexity levels to those anticipated by the authors.
Single-function generation may not reveal multi-file generation challenges, and results from 11 problems may not generalize.

We used only GPT-4.1, performance may vary with other LLMs. Our architecture requires OpenAI function-calling protocol, limiting applicability to LLMs lacking this capability (e.g., open-source models).
Limited sample size (N=11 task-level pairs) constrains statistical power, which can lead to Type II errors.
Ground truth tests might not be comprehensive.
Our evaluation focuses exclusively on functional correctness, deliberately isolating from performance, scalability, maintainability, security, and non-functional requirements in general.
Using the same LLM for test and code generation creates test-code collusion risk.
Integration of a new function does not guarantee that other functionalities remain correct.
While SelfEvolve currently operates reactively to user requests, a full MAPE architecture would enable proactive self-evolution
in mission-critical contexts, guardrails [11] need to be introduced to prevent unwanted evolutions.
